snippet.title: How did ancient civilizations brew beer? - Malcolm Purinton
snippet.description:
Trace the history and evolution of beer, from its first known existence 13,000 years ago to the modern beverage we know today.

--

Today, there are over 100 distinct beer varieties, from pilsners and bocks, to porters, stouts, and IPAs. The oldest evidence of beer brewing dates back 13,000 years, but experts believe the drink developed independently across the world. So, how did ancient civilizations brew beer, and how did their methods develop into the beverage we know today? Malcolm Purinton traces the evolution of beer.

Lesson Malcolm Purinton, directed by Anton Bogaty.

snippet.title: How a broken heart affects your body - Roni Shanoada
snippet.description:
Dig into broken heart syndrome, and find out how grief and traumatic events can affect your body and health.

--


Losing a loved one can be one of the most traumatic experiences of a person’s life. Grief brings on a whole host of strong emotions that impact both our mental and physical health. But is it possible for these powerful feelings to endanger your life? In other words, can you actually die from a broken heart? Roni Shanoada explores how traumatic events can affect your body.

Lesson by Roni Shanoada, directed by Joana Sus, NOMINT.

snippet.title: The Blood-Soaked Royal Wedding History Tried to Forget
snippet.description:
It was supposed to end a war — a royal wedding between a Catholic princess and a Protestant prince. Instead, it triggered one of the most horrifying massacres in European history.

The year was 1572. Margaret of Valois stood at the altar in Notre-Dame, marrying Henry of Navarre. But behind the music, the dancing, and the gold-stitched gowns, something darker was brewing. Four days later, the streets of Paris ran red with blood.

This wasn’t just a wedding gone wrong. It was a carefully laid trap. A celebration weaponized by power-hungry nobles and a crown desperate to survive. Thousands would die, trust would shatter, and the young couple at the heart of it all would never be the same.

Who planned the massacre? Why did the Church oppose the union? And what did Margaret do when the killing began?

This isn’t just a story of betrayal. It’s a story of control, of survival, and of a marriage forged in politics — and broken by blood.

This is the St. Bartholomew’s Day Massacre.
This is the most cursed royal wedding in history.

Every WW2 Pistol RANKED

15:42 - Hi-Power issued to both WWII sides

From the dangerously flawed Type 94 Nambu with its exposed sear bar to the legendary Browning Hi-Power GP35 carried by both Allied and Axis forces, this video ranks every major service pistol of World War II from worst to best across all theaters of the conflict. We're breaking down the full technical specs — calibers, magazine capacities, muzzle velocities, and production numbers — covering the Luger P08, Walther P38, Tokarev TT-33, M1911A1, Radom VIS 35, Beretta M1934, Enfield No. 2, and Nagant M1895, examining what made each sidearm succeed or fail in the hands of Wehrmacht infantry, Soviet officers, American Marines, and Imperial Japanese troops from the Eastern Front to the Pacific Theater. Whether you're a collector of 9mm Parabellum-chambered classics, a .45 ACP loyalist, or grinding War Thunder and Hell Let Loose and want to know which pistol your soldier would've actually trusted with his life, this deep dive covers mechanical reliability, ergonomics, cartridge performance, and battlefield effectiveness for every major nation's standard issue sidearm. The shocking truth is that some of the most iconic pistols of the war — including the visually stunning P08 — were outclassed by simpler, cheaper designs, while a Polish-made masterpiece occupied by Nazi Germany quietly earned the respect of both sides. Subscribe for more ranked military history breakdowns and comment below which WW2 pistol you think deserved the top spot.

Why European defenses and kingdoms became harder to attack

Sometimes the end of an era… isn’t destruction, but transformation.

snippet.title: Why Did the Soviet Union Really Collapse?
snippet.description:
The unraveling of a powerful empire, once seen as a global force, often holds secrets beneath the surface. What truly led to its downfall? This story isn’t just about political decisions or economic struggles; it’s about the hidden cracks that grew silently over time. Through a series of unexpected moments and bold moves, the foundation of a union that seemed unbreakable began to tremble.

As tensions rose and whispers turned into actions, what began as a collective dream soon gave way to individual aspirations for independence. Leaders found themselves at a crossroads, trying to manage a crumbling system that was no longer able to meet the needs of its people. Meanwhile, ordinary citizens felt the weight of a nation’s uncertainty bearing down on their daily lives.

Yet, amid the chaos, something unexpected emerged—small sparks of hope and defiance in the most unlikely forms. As the empire's structure weakened, it was the seemingly small acts of resistance, from humor to underground movements, that helped push the inevitable forward. What was once seen as inevitable was now unfolding in ways that no one could have predicted.

snippet.title: How Argentina Went from One of the Richest Countries to an Economic Nightmare
snippet.description:
In the early 20th century, Argentina was one of the wealthiest nations in the world, surpassing France and Germany in living standards. Buenos Aires shone with luxury, attracting immigrants from around the globe. But within a few decades, the country plunged into economic turmoil, inflation spiraled out of control, and repeated defaults shattered its financial stability. What went wrong? How did a nation once among the global elite fall into a cycle of crisis? In this video, we uncover the key moments that led to Argentina’s downfall and reveal the final blow that sealed its fate.

snippet.title: The Roman Army That Vanished Without a Trace
snippet.description:
They fought for Julius Caesar, crushed rebellions in Spain, and marched across Britain’s wild frontiers. For more than 150 years, the Ninth Legion — Legio IX Hispana — stood as one of Rome’s most battle-hardened forces. They were veterans of civil wars, conquerors of tribes, and guardians of the empire’s edge.

But then… they vanished.

One day, they are rebuilding a fortress in York. And after that — silence. No records. No orders. No explanation. A legion that had survived Caesar, Boudica, and Caledonia simply disappears into history’s fog.

Did they meet their end in the mists of Scotland? Were they redeployed to fight Jewish rebels in Judea — and destroyed in the brutal Bar Kokhba revolt? Or did their final stand come even later, on the blood-soaked frontier against the Parthians?

This wasn’t just a legion. It was a symbol of Roman endurance, loyalty, and power. And its fate remains one of antiquity’s greatest unsolved mysteries.

This is the rise, the fall, and the disappearance of the Lost Legion.

Welcome to History Blends.

snippet.title: The Rat Torture: The Most Horrifying Torture Ever Devised
snippet.description:
In the long, grim history of human cruelty, few punishments strike as deeply at our primal fears as this one. It wasn’t swift. It wasn’t merciful. It wasn’t even meant to kill—at least not at first.
This was torture designed to break a person long before their body gave out.
This was rat torture—a method so terrifying that victims often confessed before it even began.

From the dungeons of medieval Europe to the interrogation chambers of dictatorships centuries later, the idea was always the same: trap a starving rat, heat the container, and let panic do the rest. Claws. Teeth. Instinct. The animal’s fight for survival became the prisoner’s slow descent into agony. And long before flesh was torn, the mind had already shattered.

But where did this horror truly begin? How did one small creature become one of history’s most feared executioners?
Tonight, we uncover the origins of rat torture—from early accounts in ancient China and India, to the Roman culleus, to the infamous interrogations of the Dutch Revolt, and finally to the chilling reports from 20th-century secret police regimes.

Was every story real? Or did legend amplify the terror?
Join us as we follow this method across continents and centuries, tracing how an ordinary animal became a weapon of fear, humiliation, and control.
This is the true, unsettling story of the most horrifying torture ever devised.

Welcome to History Blends.

It’s a slow loris, the only venomous primate, and one of only a few venomous mammals. Despite their wide-eyed looks, their story is much fiercer than many might imagine. Stephanie A. We continue our series on the Roman Seleucid War. Taking place in the late 2nd century BC, this conflict saw the great powers of the east and west come to blows over the battlegrounds of Greece. In episode 01 we covered the lead up to the war which drew in the Romans and the Seleucids. Now we follow the unfolding carnage of their campaigns. This culminates in 191 BC where Antiochus the Greats fortifies the Hot Gates to force the Romans to attack him. Now the fate of the war will be decided at the famouse battle of Thermopylae.

snippet.title: How Medieval Peasants Cooked Without Kitchens
snippet.description:
When you picture cooking, you probably imagine a full kitchen but for most medieval peasants, that simply didn’t exist. Meals were prepared using basic tools, open fires, and shared spaces, often with very limited equipment.

In this video, we explore how ordinary people managed to cook daily meals without modern kitchens, using simple setups that were practical, efficient, and surprisingly effective.

You’ll Discover:
How open hearths were used for boiling, roasting, and baking
The role of communal ovens in villages
Simple tools like pots, spits, and cauldrons
How food was prepared with minimal space and resources
Why cooking methods were built around fire and availability

No stoves. No countertops. No appliances. Just fire, skill, and resourcefulness.

Sometimes the simplest setups… fed entire communities.
